data.title: OpenTPU – An open-source AI accelerator, developed by AI
data.author: fsbonetto
data.article_summary: openTPU是一个开源AI加速器项目，包含SystemVerilog硬件、指令集、位精确模拟器、内核编译器及PCIe主机软件，可完整展示从Python矩阵运算到芯片执行的流程。项目已在搭载Kintex-7与双DDR3的FPGA卡上运行10种模型，支持int8和4-bit量化，生成结果与模拟器逐 token 一致，最高解码速度达85.8 tok/s，DRAM带宽利用率超过90%。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI参与芯片/硬件设计及递归自我改进的可行性、性能与未来影响。

不同观点：
• 定制化路线：有人认为应将前沿模型固化进专用芯片，以降低推理成本、提升性能；但也承认还涉及芯片开发经济性、制造周期和内存带宽等物理限制。  
• FPGA与架构探索：有人推测，SOTA模型已能生成可运行模型的加速器，下一步是让AI利用大容量FPGA设计适配可重构硬件的新模型架构。  
• 实际进展派：评论称AI已参与RISC‑V核心和openTPU开发，并通过递归改进将小模型性能从几tokens/s提升至80+ tokens/s；另有人分享用AI开发开源AV1解码器。  
• 怀疑与质询：有人要求说明其硬件性能、成本及与人类设计的SOTA硬件相比是否真正提升，指出“递归自我改进”必须先证明确实能改进。  
• 开放硬件倡议：有人主张借鉴OpenAI Jalapeño，重点打造真正开源、GPU式的推理芯片，以降低采购和推理成本。  
• 社会与安全联想：有人担忧“递归自我改进会毁灭人类”、调侃SkyNet，也有人追问软件开发者未来的角色。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于当前成果究竟是实质性硬件突破，还是低成本FPGA上的早期验证；同时涉及精度可妥协（LLM未必需要严格浮点运算）与工程可靠性的权衡。

openTPU
An open-source AI accelerator, developed by AI.
openTPU brings the lessons of
auto-arch-tournament
to AI accelerators. It asks two questions: how far can AI agents go at hardware design, and can
they build the chip that runs their own inference?
otpu-chat
running LFM2.5-230M on the FPGA card (left), with
otpu-smi
showing the card's
utilization and DRAM bandwidth (right).
A place to learn
openTPU is also a learning project. The whole accelerator lives in one small monorepo that you
can read end to end: the hardware design (SystemVerilog), the instruction set, a bit-exact
simulator, a kernel language and its compiler, and the host software that drives a real PCIe
card. If you want to understand how an AI accelerator works, from a matmul in Python down to
the wires, this is a good place to start.
Results
The design runs ten modern models with their real weights on an Inspur YPCB-00338 card
(Xilinx Kintex-7 xc7k480t, two DDR3 channels), and the card produces the same tokens as the
simulator, bit for bit.

Measured on the card: the first three models on 2026-09-29 with the production image
deploy_champ_e698dcd7
. LFM2-2.6B, SmolLM3-3B and Phi-4-mini on 2026-09-30, and Qwen3.5-2B and
4B and Gemma 4 on 2026-10-01, with build B,
deploy_fused133c_79c5707a
, production since then.
Build B decodes LFM2-2.6B, SmolLM3 and Phi-4-mini 8-9% faster than e698dcd7 (Gemma 4 E2B 10%),
at 91-94% of the DRAM peak instead of 82-87%. Qwen3.5-4B's int8 image is over 4 GiB.
The image: main e698dcd at 133.33 MHz, one bitstream for all models. It has LiteDRAM
controllers calibrated by a small CPU inside the memory core, a four-column systolic matrix
unit and the stream engine (
docs/stream.md
). DDR3-1066, with a 17.1 GB/s
peak.
The host: the card sits in opentpu (Intel Core i7-4790).
Method,
tools/qual/perf.py
: decode is 64 greedy tokens after a 512-token prompt, with the
host's argmax in the loop (not streamed). "Device" counts only the cycles the accelerator runs;
"wall" adds the host. Prefill is the 512-token prompt, on the device.
DRAM traffic comes from the card's own counters while it runs.
Gemma 4 E2B keeps its per-layer embedding tables on the card (3.5-3.6 GiB images;
docs/gemma4.md
); in int8 it does not fit. It matches Hugging Face's greedy
tokens on three prompts with either head. E4B's table (2.95 GB) stays on the host, which
copies one 11 KB row into the card per token; its image is 3.96 GiB, int8 with the head and
the first 24 layers' down projections in 4-bit (
docs/gemma4_e4b.md
).
In the card's own decode loop (the card picking every token) Gemma 4 decodes faster: E2B
11.01 / 12.73 tok/s (int8 / 4-bit head), E4B 3.83 tok/s, on the device.
Every configuration matches the simulator token for token, per-position and with the
resident decode program. More detail in
docs/board.md
.
With the logits streamed back while the card runs (
tools/decode_profile.py
, 96 tokens), 4-bit
decode is faster, in device / wall tok/s:

Qwen3: 33.7 / 33.3;

data.title: The Early History of Smalltalk (1993)
data.author: _reza
data.article_summary: 文章回顾了Smalltalk从20世纪60年代至80年代的发展历程及思想来源。它受分时计算、图形界面、Sketchpad、Simula、LISP、LOGO等影响，在Xerox PARC逐步形成面向对象、消息传递、窗口和个人计算等理念。Smalltalk旨在适应计算机性能指数增长和大众使用需求，最终成为现代个人计算、图形用户界面及面向对象编程的重要范例。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Smalltalk的历史影响、语言理念、实践价值，以及其未能成为主流的原因。

不同观点：
• **历史影响深远**：Smalltalk深刻影响了NeXTSTEP、Objective-C、Interface Builder和Xcode；其消息传递、动态性和图形化对象序列化等理念延续至今。它还影响了面向对象教育、Logo及早期个人计算机思想。  
• **语言体验优雅**：使用者称赞其语法简洁、以对象为核心，并能让程序员“生活在程序中”；相比Java，Smalltalk的集合等机制更自然，Ruby也带来类似愉悦。  
• **技术先进但商业失败**：有人认为Smalltalk本应胜出，但因运行速度、硬件支持不足、供应商倒闭、生态和成本问题失势。实际项目后来转向免费且快速的C++，或Java、JavaScript、Visual Basic；企业还认为Smalltalk开发者成本过高。  
• **对其优越性的反思**：也有人指出，Smalltalk爱好者容易沉溺于怀旧、持续批评现代工具；“技术先进”并不等于普及成功。  
• **持续存活**：尽管不主流，Instantiations等公司仍持续发布Smalltalk，客户也在长期使用。

补充讨论：评论通过Alan Kay访谈、Smalltalk早期史及OOP历史资料展开追溯；争议焦点是语言的先进性与商业可行性、人才成本和生态普及之间的矛盾。ข้อความเต็ม.

Abstract
Most ideas come from previous ideas.  The sixties, particularly in the ARPA
community, gave rise to a host of notions about "human-computer symbiosis"
through interactive time-shared computers, graphics screens and pointing
devices. Advanced computer languages were invented to simulate complex systems
such as oil refineries and semi-intelligent behavior.  The soon-to-follow paradigm
shift of modern personal computing, overlapping window interfaces, and
object-oriented design came from seeing the work of the sixties as something
more than a "better old thing."  That is, more than a better way: to do mainframe
computing; for end-users to invoke functionality; to make data structures more
abstract.  Instead the promise of exponential growth in computing/$/volume
demanded that the sixties be regarded as "
almost
a new thing" and to find out
what the actual "new things" might be.  For example, one would compute with a
handheld "Dynabook" in a way that would not be possible on a shared mainframe;
millions of potential users meant that the user interface would have to
become a learning environment along the lines of Montessori and Bruner; and
needs for large scope, reduction in complexity, and end-user literacy would
require that data and control structures be done away with in favor of a more
biological scheme of protected universal cells interacting only through messages
that could mimic any desired behavior.
Early Smalltalk was the first complete realization of these new points of view
as parented by its many predecessors in hardware, language and user interface
design.  It became the exemplar of the new computing, in part, because we were
actually trying for a qualitative shift in belief structures—a new Kuhnian paradigm
in the same spirit as the invention of the printing press—and thus took
highly extreme positions which almost forced these new styles to be invented.

Introduction
I'm writing this introduction in an airplane at 35,000 feet.  On my lap is a five pound
notebook computer—1992's "Interim Dynabook"—by the end of the year it sold for under $700.  It
has a flat, crisp, high-resolution bitmap screen, overlapping windows, icons, a pointing device,
considerable storage and computing capacity, and its best software is object-oriented.  It has
advanced networking built-in and there are already options for wireless networking.
Smalltalk runs on this system, and is one of the main systems I use for my current work with
children.  In some ways this is more than a Dynabook (quantitatively), and some ways not
quite there yet (qualitatively).  All in all, pretty much what was in mind during the late sixties.
Smalltalk was part of this larger pursuit of ARPA, and later of Xerox PARC, that I called
personal
computing.
There were so many people involved in each stage from the research communities
that the accurate allocation of credit for ideas is intractably difficult.  Instead, as Bob Barton
liked to quote Goethe, we should "share in the excitement of discovery without

data.title: Benchmark in Milliseconds
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章建议将微基准测试调整到约300毫秒：低于10毫秒容易受启动等固定开销影响，数百毫秒则能减少偶发误差且便于人直观感受性能差异；超过1秒又会拖慢迭代和多次运行。基准测试的重点不是极精确测量，而是帮助作者形成足够直觉并做出正确决策。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何设计可信、可复现且适合不同场景的性能基准测试。

不同观点：
• **统计严谨派**：应在同一轮测试中交替测量基准与对照，重复多轮并报告95%置信区间，而非只看平均值；区间重叠时不能轻易断言更快。Tachometer采用了类似方法。  
• **场景与长期稳定派**：测试时长取决于目标。Python、Java需考虑启动成本、GC、JIT预热；数据库、游戏还要测稳态、长时间运行、内存泄漏和第25分钟后的掉帧，短微基准不能代表整体性能。  
• **快速实用派**：在寻找3倍、10倍等明显收益时，短测或凭体感即可；有人建议多次短跑并取最快结果，以减少无关活动干扰，但这与统计派的“使用分布和置信区间”存在争议。  
• **工程经验派**：应使用成熟框架而非自制标准，如Criterion、JMH、BenchmarkDotNet、Rust基准工具；JMH通过预热、JVM分叉、Blackhole等避免JIT和优化误差。  
• **硬件与时间尺度派**：CPU调频、系统中断、SMI会造成不可复现的抖动；浏览器计时精度要求通常运行50–100ms。不同任务可能更适合微秒、毫秒或秒级指标。

补充讨论：核心争议是“足够快、直观”与“统计可靠、可复现”的取舍；测试时长、输入代表性和是否取最快值，应依据优化目标与噪声水平调整。

49967427.article_content:
How long should a micro benchmark run? My rule of thumb is to tweak the input
size until the benchmark takes about 300ms, for the following reasons:
Milliseconds are integers ranging from 1 to 999. Enough precision to notice
even a small improvement, and easy to scan visually. No need for different
units or floating points (compare
1.31s
with
239ms
).
Anything faster than, say,
10ms
risks being skewed by fixed costs (e.g,
interpreter startup). Hundreds of milliseconds is an eternity for a computer,
usually enough to make one-off overheads irrelevant without using fancier (=
less robust) techniques to explicitly account for them.
For a human, hundreds of milliseconds is fast, but noticeable. Pushing numbers
into human-perceptible range allows me to use my intuitive sense of time and
speed, it doesn’t rely exclusively on numeracy. It’s plain fun to see, as a
result of optimization work, how a previously lagging CLI command becomes
“instant”.
But anything longer than a second makes
iterating
on the benchmark slower
than it needs to be. Running a benchmark 10 times in a row to eyeball variance
should be fast!
The imminently-to-be-stated assumption here is that the purpose of benchmarking
isn’t so much a precise measurement of performance, but rather providing the
author with enough intuition to make a correct decision.
49967427.article_summary: 文章建议将微基准测试调整到约300毫秒：低于10毫秒容易受启动等固定开销影响，数百毫秒则能减少偶发误差且便于人直观感受性能差异；超过1秒又会拖慢迭代和多次运行。基准测试的重点不是极精确测量，而是帮助作者形成足够直觉并做出正确决策。
49967427.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何设计可信、可复现且适合不同场景的性能基准测试。

不同观点：
• **统计严谨派**：应在同一轮测试中交替测量基准与对照，重复多轮并报告95%置信区间，而非只看平均值；区间重叠时不能轻易断言更快。Tachometer采用了类似方法。  
• **场景与长期稳定派**：测试时长取决于目标。Python、Java需考虑启动成本、GC、JIT预热；数据库、游戏还要测稳态、长时间运行、内存泄漏和第25分钟后的掉帧，短微基准不能代表整体性能。  
• **快速实用派**：在寻找3倍、10倍等明显收益时，短测或凭体感即可；有人建议多次短跑并取最快结果，以减少无关活动干扰，但这与统计派的“使用分布和置信区间”存在争议。  
• **工程经验派**：应使用成熟框架而非自制标准，如Criterion、JMH、BenchmarkDotNet、Rust基准工具；JMH通过预热、JVM分叉、Blackhole等避免JIT和优化误差。  
• **硬件与时间尺度派**：CPU调频、系统中断、SMI会造成不可复现的抖动；浏览器计时精度要求通常运行50–100ms。不同任务可能更适合微秒、毫秒或秒级指标。

补充讨论：核心争议是“足够快、直观”与“统计可靠、可复现”的取舍；测试时长、输入代表性和是否取最快值，应依据优化目标与噪声水平调整。

data.title: Sharing AI progress in mathematics
data.author: OfficialTurkey
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI 数学系统声称解决大量长期开放问题，其成果的数学重要性、可信度及对未来研究的影响。

不同观点：
• **重大突破论**：有人认为解决唯一游戏猜想、黎曼/霍奇相关问题、Barnette 猜想等，可能相当于数十年甚至50—100年的人类数学进展；若成果属实，历史意义非凡。  
• **具体成果认可论**：评论者关注可理解或应用明确的问题，如三机调度、图论、图灵度刚性、整数乘法、平面染色等，并赞叹推理轨迹、Lean 形式化验证及较低计算成本。  
• **谨慎怀疑论**：部分人尚无法核查证明，指出调度结果虽声称多项式算法，却有极大的指数 \(150020\)，且采用较不自然的图灵机模型；因此“解决”仍需专家复核。  
• **技术跃迁论**：有人认为这是数学史上罕见的加速，体现 AI 汇聚现代数学知识的能力；也有人借此追问 AI 是否会持续进步、是否可能影响更广泛领域。  
• **人文与价值观点**：有人反对把成果单纯看作竞争，强调 AI 揭示的是原本就存在的数学之美；另有“AI 加速发展令人担忧”的立场，关注其社会后果。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于证明的独立验证、成果的实际数学深度与影响，以及“解决90题”是否等同于真正推进数学；评论还反复比较理论重要性与问题排名。

data.title: Penguin Mail – open-source Rust email client for Linux with AI
data.author: kavourias
data.article_summary: Penguin Mail是一款面向Linux的免费开源邮件与日历客户端，支持Gmail、Microsoft、IMAP和POP3账户，统一管理邮件、日历与联系人。提供托盘同步、通知、规则、定时发送、撤回、OpenPGP/S/MIME加密及可选本地AI助手。应用无自有服务器、无广告和追踪，数据主要保留在用户电脑上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款用 Rust/GTK 开发的原生 Linux 邮件客户端，评论集中讨论其界面与定位、功能完整性、AI设计、稳定性及生态适配。

不同观点：
• 肯定者认为界面美观，有 Mail.app 或 Sparrow 的感觉；原生 Linux 邮件客户端较少，且软件定制成本下降有助于形成面向不同群体的多样化产品。
• 质疑“1.0”定位者认为项目仅开发约一个月，邮件客户端复杂度高，日历等功能可能存在需长期使用才能暴露的 bug，称其为稳定版过早。
• 反感 AI 者表示看到“with AI”就失去兴趣，尤其不喜欢内嵌聊天窗口；更倾向提供 CLI，让用户自行接入代理并查询邮件。
• 功能体验批评者在 Fastmail 测试后指出：无法选择发件人地址、缺少邮件 favicon、文件夹排序混乱、文件夹着色受服务器限制，整体 UI 仍需打磨。
• 工程与扩展性关注者询问测试方法、复杂功能的 bug 覆盖及沙箱方案，并希望有 TUI 版本和其他操作系统支持。

补充讨论：争议焦点包括 AI 是否必要、项目是否具备宣布 1.0 的成熟度，以及功能便利性与安全、可扩展性之间的取舍。另有人提醒行业惯例是在标题后注明“written in Rust”。

49984716.article_content:
Penguin Mail
Mail and calendar for Linux
Gmail, Microsoft and any IMAP or POP3 account, with your calendar and contacts, in one fast app on your own computer.
Download
Source on GitHub
Version 1.0.0.
Free software under GPL-3.0-or-later, for x86_64 Linux.
Enlarge
Enlarge
Every account in one inbox, in light or dark to match your system.
Enlarge
The calendar, beside your mail.
What it does
Gmail, Microsoft, IMAP and POP3 accounts
Sign in to Gmail, to Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live or Microsoft 365, or to Fastmail, iCloud, Yahoo or any IMAP, POP3 and SMTP server. Penguin Mail finds the server settings from your address.
One inbox, synced from the tray
Read every account in one inbox or one at a time. Penguin Mail keeps syncing from the system tray, with an unread count and notifications you can act on.
Your calendar
Day, Week, Month and Agenda views of every calendar on every account: Google, Microsoft, and CalDAV where your provider offers it. Answer an invitation from the message it came in.
Contacts
Your contacts from Google, Microsoft, or CardDAV where your provider offers it, and suggestions from the people you write to as you type a recipient.
OpenPGP and S/MIME
Sign and encrypt through your own GnuPG. Penguin Mail never holds your keys or asks for a passphrase.
Rules
Gmail filters, Microsoft inbox rules, and Sieve rules where your provider offers them, listed in plain words, with a form to add one.
An optional assistant
Off until you choose a model. It can run on your own computer, through LM Studio or Ollama, and it asks before it sends mail or changes a setting.
A closer look
Enlarge
Ask your mail a question
Press Ctrl+J and ask which sent mail is still waiting on a reply, or what is in your promotions. The assistant reads your mailboxes with the app's own tools and shows each one it ran.
Enlarge
An inbox split the way Gmail splits it
A bar above the list sorts mail into Primary, Updates, Promotions and Social, using Gmail's own categories. Move a sender to another category and it stays there.
Enlarge
Send it later, or take it back
Schedule a message for Monday morning and it goes out on time while Penguin Mail runs, even from the tray. Sent mail waits a few seconds with an Undo button first.
Enlarge
An address for every sign-up
Hide My Email makes a Gmail plus address for each site you join. When one of them starts getting spam, turn that address off and its mail goes to the Trash.
Your mail stays on your computer
Penguin Mail has no server of its own, no tracking and no ads. Gmail and Google Calendar accounts talk to Google directly, and Microsoft accounts talk to Microsoft Graph, so no other server sees your mail.
Read the privacy policy
Watch the tour
A two-minute video on YouTube.

data.title: AnyPS5: Port PS5 binaries to PC without emulation (87% system libraries mapped)
data.author: Fe2O3
data.article_summary: 该项目是一个开源工具，可将PS5可执行文件自动移植到Linux和Windows。它通过重链接器转换原生格式，并提供可动态链接的系统PRX库，无需模拟器或独立运行时。项目支持Vulkan着色器重编译、手柄及键鼠输入，已有少量游戏验证运行。采用GPLv2许可证，强调研究、兼容与软件保存用途。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕主机游戏逆向、移植与本地运行的技术价值、法律风险，以及其对游戏平台和软件产业的影响。

不同观点：
• **支持保存与反垄断**：认为 AI 降低逆向门槛、促进游戏本地运行和跨平台移植，有助于避免厂商锁定；即使项目可能被下架，也应保留 Git 镜像或本地备份，Yuzu、Ryujinx 被法律手段清除就是例子。  
• **担忧厂商转向云游戏**：逆向和破解能力增强可能促使 Sony、任天堂、微软进一步推动云端游玩，以限制本地复制和修改，最终削弱玩家对游戏的实际所有权。  
• **质疑商业与产业后果**：有人认为若游戏首发即被破解，玩家可能不再付费，像 GTA 6 等大作及软件产业将受到冲击；也有人以“你将一无所有但会很快乐”讽刺数字所有权的弱化。  
• **关注开发者风险**：项目作者通常解决的是有趣且复杂的技术问题，但一旦过于流行，可能遭遇政府或版权方调查、诉讼和项目下架。  
• **技术讨论**：有人询问其是否类似 WINE 的兼容层方案；另有观点指出 PS5 已采用 x86-64，难点或不在 CPU 翻译，而在专有图形 API，重点是如何将 GNM 命令缓冲预编译为 Vulkan，以及是否仍需运行时拦截。

补充讨论：评论整体在“技术创新与文化保存”同“版权执法、商业可持续性和平台控制”之间存在明显张力。

data.title: Decisions API is in public beta
data.author: chiefstorm
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Decisions API：可处理文本、图像或两者，以约10倍于 Responses API 的速度返回结构化判断。支持 predicate（条件概率）、choice（固定选项）和 score（有序评分）三类问题，用于分类、路由和任务排序。目前处于公开测试阶段，仅支持 gpt-6-luna，调用 POST /v1/decisions。需要自定义 JSON 或工具调用时，应使用 Responses API 的 Structured Outputs 或函数调用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 推出 Decisions API，用于快速输出分类/置信度等结构化判断，引发对模型性能、价格、行业竞争及产品定位的讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好速度与低成本**：支持者认为简单的是非判断无需完整生成，Decisions 比 Responses API 快约10倍，价格相近，质量可能持平；Jev 已证明“System One”模型和专用决策接口的价值，AI 服务或进一步陷入价格竞争。  
• **质疑竞争力**：Topfi 的实测显示，Decisions 比 Jev 慢约3.1倍、价格更高、失败调用更多，在其 UI、知识管理等任务中置信度和能力较弱；整体像是仓促跟进，需更多基准测试。  
• **强调多模态优势**：相较 Jev，Decisions 支持图像输入，可能适合识别凹痕、界面元素，甚至实时游戏；语音决策也被认为有潜力。  
• **主张本地或开源替代**：评论推荐可在 CPU 上运行的开源分类器及 gutsy，以降低成本和供应商依赖。  
• **质疑独立 API 形态**：有人认为决策路由应直接整合进通用模型或后训练流程，以提升校准输出，而非作为单独接口。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“专用决策模型是否真正带来速度、成本或质量优势”，以及 OpenAI 是否只是在跟随 Jev。用户还期待基准测试，并关注未来各大模型厂商的跟进。

The Decisions API evaluates text, images, or both and returns typed answers about 10x faster than the Responses API. Get the probability that a condition is true, a choice from a fixed set, or a score against a rubric. Use those answers to classify content, route requests, and prioritize work in your application.
Try the Decisions API in the
Playground
to experiment with questions and inputs before writing code.
The Decisions API is in public beta, and we expect to GA in the coming weeks.
gpt-6-luna
is the only model currently available. Use the dedicated
POST   /v1/decisions
endpoint.
How decisions work
A request has three parts:

gpt-6-luna
is supported.
input
Shared evidence for the questions: a text string or user messages containing text and images.
questions

The response contains an
answers

name

Choose a question type

Main result
predicate

probability

choice

Rate an input against ordered levels, such as issue severity.
score

Both

and
score
return probabilities over discrete options. Use
choice
for categories without an order, such as departments. Use
score
for ordered levels, such as severity; it takes the probability-weighted average of their numeric indices to produce a score that can fall between levels.
Use Decisions when your application needs one of these answer types. Use
Structured Outputs
with the Responses API when you need to generate an object that follows your own JSON schema, such as extracted fields or a written explanation, or

49984025.article_summary: 文章介绍了 Decisions API：可处理文本、图像或两者，以约10倍于 Responses API 的速度返回结构化判断。支持 predicate（条件概率）、choice（固定选项）和 score（有序评分）三类问题，用于分类、路由和任务排序。目前处于公开测试阶段，仅支持 gpt-6-luna，调用 POST /v1/decisions。需要自定义 JSON 或工具调用时，应使用 Responses API 的 Structured Outputs 或函数调用。
49984025.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI 推出 Decisions API，用于快速输出分类/置信度等结构化判断，引发对模型性能、价格、行业竞争及产品定位的讨论。

不同观点：
• **看好速度与低成本**：支持者认为简单的是非判断无需完整生成，Decisions 比 Responses API 快约10倍，价格相近，质量可能持平；Jev 已证明“System One”模型和专用决策接口的价值，AI 服务或进一步陷入价格竞争。  
• **质疑竞争力**：Topfi 的实测显示，Decisions 比 Jev 慢约3.1倍、价格更高、失败调用更多，在其 UI、知识管理等任务中置信度和能力较弱；整体像是仓促跟进，需更多基准测试。  
• **强调多模态优势**：相较 Jev，Decisions 支持图像输入，可能适合识别凹痕、界面元素，甚至实时游戏；语音决策也被认为有潜力。  
• **主张本地或开源替代**：评论推荐可在 CPU 上运行的开源分类器及 gutsy，以降低成本和供应商依赖。  
• **质疑独立 API 形态**：有人认为决策路由应直接整合进通用模型或后训练流程，以提升校准输出，而非作为单独接口。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“专用决策模型是否真正带来速度、成本或质量优势”，以及 OpenAI 是否只是在跟随 Jev。用户还期待基准测试，并关注未来各大模型厂商的跟进。

data.author: ilreb
data.article_summary: Google DeepMind发布EmbeddingGemma 2，一款基于Gemma 4、740亿？ No, 7.4亿参数的开源轻量多模态嵌入模型，采用Apache 2.0许可，可将文本、代码、图像、音频和视频映射至统一向量空间。模型支持模块化配置、向量压缩、8K上下文，适合手机端离线搜索、跨模态检索和RAG，兼顾隐私、低延迟与较高性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EmbeddingGemma 2 的开放许可、模型规模、多模态能力、部署方式及性能比较。

不同观点：
• **支持开放模型**：Apache 2.0 和开放权重让用户可长期掌控模型；即使托管商停止服务，也能自行部署或更换供应商，避免数百万向量重新嵌入的成本与风险。  
• **看好中等规模与多模态**：270M 文本、440M 文本+视觉（总参数拆分还包括音频，约740M）的规模适合本地运行，弥补了中等尺寸嵌入模型不足；可用于文本、图像及“Jev”类跨模态任务。  
• **关注压缩与部署限制**：有人指出该模型采用 MRL，而非 MatFormer，因此只能压缩向量维度，不能同步缩小模型权重；也有人询问二值量化是否兼容。  
• **性能仍需验证**：有人希望与 Voyage、SigLIP2、Qwen 等模型公平比较；当前文本基准据称与第一代相当，但多模态准确率、幻觉率和实际设备表现仍缺少数据。  
• **期待应用落地**：评论者计划将其加入测试框架、加速本地向量生成，并期待用于 RAG transformations。

补充讨论：争议焦点主要是模型压缩方案、与其他模型的可比性，以及多模态能力在真实场景中的实际收益。

We introduced
EmbeddingGemma
last year to provide a lightweight option for high-quality text embeddings, to help your apps organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware. The developer community’s response blew past our expectations. With more than 20 million downloads, builders have used it to power smarter on-device search tools and privacy-first retrieval augmented generation (RAG) pipelines.
Today, we’re launching EmbeddingGemma 2
,
expanding beyond text to unify code, images, video, and audio in a shared embedding space. Built on the Gemma 4 architecture and released under a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license, EmbeddingGemma 2 has 740 million parameters, making it optimal for on-device inference. It can help find a specific video clip from a voice memo, or search through hours of audio recordings based on a text query, all processed by a single, natively multimodal model.
Built from the same technology as Gemini Embedding models, EmbeddingGemma 2 is:
Best-in-class for its size:
Achieves leading scores among sub-1B multimodal embedders for its size across benchmarks like MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) Code and MAEB (Massive Audio Embedding Benchmark), while matching or outperforming many larger models across text, vision, and audio tasks.
Modular by design:
Requires as little as 270M parameters for text-only workloads with optional vision (170M) and audio (300M) encoders for full multimodal support.
Storage-efficient:
Using Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL), developers can dynamically truncate output vectors from 768 dimensions down to 512, 256, or 128 dimensions. This provides up to 6x storage reduction for local vector databases and memory usage.
Optimized for on-device performance:
Runs efficiently within tight resource constraints. With quantization, on a Google Pixel 11 Pro, EmbeddingGemma 2 requires as little as ~191MB active RAM for text-only weights and ~567MB for the full multimodal model.
Extended context ready:
Features an 8K token context window (4x larger than EmbeddingGemma 1), allowing it to process up to 5.5 minutes of audio, 29 images, 58 video frames, or interleaved combinations thereof directly on local hardware.
Achieving top-tier quality for code, vision, and audio
EmbeddingGemma 2 matches the strong multilingual text performance of EmbeddingGemma while delivering a significant 9.92-point improvement on code performance (in MTEB Code, from 68.76 to 78.68), making it well-suited for local codebase indexing, semantic code search, and coding agent retrieval. Across image, video, documents, and audio, it sets a new standard in quality-per-parameter for sub-1B models and even outperforms some specialist models more than twice its size.
Find full evaluation metrics and model information in the
EmbeddingGemma 2 model card
.
Enabling semantic search, routing, and retrieval, fully on-device
EmbeddingGemma 2 brings robust capabilities directly to edge hardware. Generating embeddings locally helps ensure data privacy, reduces pipeline latency, and empowers developers to build cross-modal search and retrieval that works entirely offline.
When paired with generative models such as Gemma 4, EmbeddingGemma 2 enables on-device RAG pipelines that understand complex multimodal data. Because EmbeddingGemma 2 is built on Gemma 4 and shares its text tokenizer and audio encoder, developers can run both models together in a unified pipeline with a lower combined total memory footprint.

data.title: Integer multiplication below n log n
data.author: E-Reverance
data.article_summary: 目前提供的信息仅包含论文题目、作者、日期及文件列表，未包含正文内容，因此无法准确总结其主要结论。论文题为《Integer multiplication below n log n》，主题应与低于 \(n\log n\) 复杂度的整数乘法算法有关，但具体方法、证明和结果仍需查看 paper.pdf。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：评论围绕一种略低于 \(n\log n\) 的整数乘法复杂度结果展开，重点讨论其理论意义、可信度及实际价值。

不同观点：
• **理论突破派**：认为即使只削减极其微小的复杂度，也意味着突破了长期的 \(n\log n\) 阈值，可能为后续更大改进打开空间；数学结构本身也很值得欣赏。  
• **审慎怀疑派**：质疑论文是否有 Lean 等机器检验证明。鉴于大模型可能自信地产出错误或细微错误的论证，在缺乏充分人工核查前不应轻信，甚至有人希望结果是错的，因为简洁的 \(n\log n\) 更“漂亮”。  
• **实际应用派**：指出改进幅度极小，只有面对规模至少约 \(2^{118000}\) 的数组才可能体现意义，现实中几乎不会关心，除非算法能真正泛化。  
• **数学与AI讨论派**：惊叹需要价值数万亿美元的AI技术才发现乘法的新改进，同时强调数学远未被大模型“解决”，仍有大量深层开放问题。  
• **幽默调侃派**：调侃 \(n\log n^{(1-2^{-182})}\) 的微小改进、PDF格式以及AI是否主动投入了额外推理时间。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“微小理论突破是否足够重要”以及“AI生成结果在缺乏机器验证时是否可信”；评论者普遍认可其潜在理论价值，但对可读性、可验证性和实际收益存疑。

data.author: zed_labs_dev
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM聊天界面展示“预测的用户下一条消息”究竟是训练副产物、产品功能，还是影响用户行为的数据采集手段。

不同观点：
• 机制解释：LLM因“预测下一个token”的训练方式，能自然生成类似用户提问的内容；该能力可能早已存在，只是近期才开放展示，并非专门为获取训练数据而设计。  
• 质疑训练必要性：即使不展示预测，也可让模型预测下一条消息，再与用户真实输入比较训练，因此公开建议未必能改善训练；展示的真正作用可能是引导用户下一步输入。  
• 用户体验反感：有人厌恶自动替用户补全句子；也有人指出建议语句常用全小写，且自己从未采用。  
• 隐私与商业担忧：付费或企业用户原以为提示不会用于训练，担心实验室通过隐蔽功能重新获取数据，进而形成少数公司对高质量使用数据的垄断。  
• 其他推测：有人建议直接预生成回复；另有评论称产品开始主动询问“Claude做得如何”，可能在收集满意度反馈。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“展示预测”究竟服务于模型训练、用户引导还是反馈采集；评论还延伸到AI公司是否优先服务未来的AI体系，而非人类用户。

主要讨论点：LLM聊天界面展示“预测的用户下一条消息”究竟是训练副产物、产品功能，还是影响用户行为的数据采集手段。

不同观点：
• 机制解释：LLM因“预测下一个token”的训练方式，能自然生成类似用户提问的内容；该能力可能早已存在，只是近期才开放展示，并非专门为获取训练数据而设计。  
• 质疑训练必要性：即使不展示预测，也可让模型预测下一条消息，再与用户真实输入比较训练，因此公开建议未必能改善训练；展示的真正作用可能是引导用户下一步输入。  
• 用户体验反感：有人厌恶自动替用户补全句子；也有人指出建议语句常用全小写，且自己从未采用。  
• 隐私与商业担忧：付费或企业用户原以为提示不会用于训练，担心实验室通过隐蔽功能重新获取数据，进而形成少数公司对高质量使用数据的垄断。  
• 其他推测：有人建议直接预生成回复；另有评论称产品开始主动询问“Claude做得如何”，可能在收集满意度反馈。

补充讨论：争议焦点是“展示预测”究竟服务于模型训练、用户引导还是反馈采集；评论还延伸到AI公司是否优先服务未来的AI体系，而非人类用户。

data.title: State of Devs 2026 survey results: developers are exhausted
data.author: sgdesign
data.article_summary: 2026年开发者调查显示，行业前景充满不确定性：近半数受访者经历过工作不稳定或收入不足，超过四分之一担心未来五年被迫转行。约三分之二出现动力下降、愤世嫉俗等倦怠迹象，62%曾经历职业倦怠。AI使用普遍但评价两极分化，近半数认为其未改善心理状态，并可能带来学习削弱与认知过载。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕科技行业从业者调查数据的解读，涉及行业前景、职业稳定性、样本偏差，以及管理与人才培养问题。

不同观点：
• **相对乐观**：benoau指出，尽管整体数据令人悲观，仍有两点积极信号：约50%的人认为未来五年不太可能或很不可能转行，42%的人对科技行业感到希望或兴奋。  
• **对数据有效性的质疑**：woah关注调查可能存在的选择偏差，认为参与者构成或调查渠道可能影响结论，因此不能直接将结果视为整个行业的真实状况。  
• **对行业和管理文化的系统性批评**：austin-cheney认为“能力不足却不断晋升”的现象正在触及极限，许多管理者缺乏技术经验，甚至存在失职、权责混乱和有毒领导。他以自身遭遇为例，说明糟糕管理可能导致员工被错误解雇。其进一步批评非软件公司的开发组织：人才培养不足、开发者被当作可快速替换的“商品”，低门槛培训与高薪造成能力和职业安全感错配，并使问题延续到下一代管理层。  
• **情绪性反应**：anramon仅表示标题本身就令人疲惫，反映出读者对该话题沉重基调的直观感受。

补充讨论：核心争议在于，调查呈现的悲观情绪究竟源于行业真实危机，还是样本偏差；同时也存在对austin-cheney关于“多数开发者能力不足”等广泛概括是否过度绝对化的隐含争议。

data.title: UniEvo-VL: Self-Distillation Training for Multimodal Model Self-Improvement
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 文章提出UniEvo-VL，一种多模态模型的在策略自蒸馏自进化框架。模型同时充当教师与学生：教师利用自我批评等特权信息，学生仅接收原始问题，通过对齐扩散生成分布学习自我纠错。实验表明，该方法显著提升图像生成性能（GenEval由0.747升至0.808），且无需外部监督；更强的评审器可进一步提高上限，但不同任务上的改进并不均衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕模型训练方法、基准测试有效性，以及通过蒸馏和扩展参数提升训练潜力的设想展开。

不同观点：
• **对评测结果的质疑**：schopra909认为 GenEval/GenEval2 的提示词仅约10个词，而模型主要用长而密集的描述进行训练，短提示可能属于分布外输入。将提示词扩写后再评测，更能反映模型真实能力。其引用 Qwen-Image 报告称，扩写提示得分可达0.87；论文则通过方法将分数从0.74提升到0.81，因此可能只是让模型适应基准提示，而非真正提升能力。
• **对方法必要性的疑问**：上述评论进一步指出，尚不清楚针对短提示直接微调，是否能达到与强化学习方案相同的效果，争议焦点在于性能提升来自模型能力增强，还是来自评测分布适配。
• **循环蒸馏与权重拆分设想**：Lerc提出模型训练饱和后，先蒸馏成四分之一规模，再扩展回原规模；通过将权重拆分为 W1+W2=W，并加入随机偏移，使层宽翻倍、参数量扩大，从而获得更大的继续训练空间。该观点目前属于假设，尚未提供实验验证。

补充讨论：两条评论都关注训练技巧是否带来真实泛化能力，而非仅优化特定测试设置；前者侧重评测公平性，后者侧重突破模型容量或训练饱和。

View a PDF of the paper titled UniEvo-VL: An On-policy Self-Distillation Training Recipe for Multimodal Model Self-improvement, by Fang Wu and 18 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Modern multimodal models bring generation and understanding into a single unified system, which enables them to provide and learn from their own feedback. Motivated by this unified capacity, we introduce UniEvo-VL, a self-evolving framework for multimodal models to learn from this constructive self-correction feedback during test-time compute. Instead of relying on a separate, often larger, teacher, we leverage their self-critiques as privileged information and ask a single multimodal model to act as both teacher and student with different contexts. The student only sees the vanilla question, while the teacher conditions on the privileged critique. Then training minimizes the per-state divergence between their denoising diffusion distributions over the student's own sampling trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that UniEvo-VL improves the image generation capabilities of multimodal models, while maintaining their sensitivity to additional reflection information. Specifically, we build on top of the open-source Qwen-image-2512 and observe a significant performance gain from 0.747 to 0.808 on GenEval and from 32.97 to 35.53 on GenEval2 Soft-TIFA. Moreover, attempts with more powerful external critics (e.g., GPT5.6-Luna) show that multimodal models with strong judge capabilities can anticipate a higher self-evolving ceiling. Last but not least, mixed text-rendering outcomes show that our self-improvements may not be uniform across different tasks. Our study aims to shed light on the current hot recursive self-improvement research line to enhance the user experience when using multimodal models without external supervision or guidance.

data.title: When random is not actually random enough
data.author: steveklabnik
data.article_summary: 文章指出，用随机数对选项数取模会产生偏差：当随机数范围不能被选项数整除时，各对象被选中的概率不相等。应使用能保证均匀分布的 `random_between`（如拒绝采样），并优先提供明确表达概率分布的 `random_choice` 接口，以支持均匀或加权选择；实际实现可采用相对整数权重，避免浮点数误差。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何正确、易用地生成均匀随机数，以及随机数 API 的抽象层级与质量检测。

不同观点：
• **取模会产生偏差**：wilbo指出，`random_u64() % 3`因样本空间不能被3整除，会使某个选项略微过度出现（约 \(5×10^{-20}\)）；而`rand()`仅有32767种取值，在分桶数量不合适时偏差可能更明显。  
• **应采用拒绝采样**：tialaramex认为，生成指定范围整数的正确方法是拒绝采样：先生成足够大的随机值，落在目标范围内则接受，否则丢弃并重试。例如用半字节生成2到11之间的数。其强调随机数并非稀缺资源，简单实现反而更易维护和验证。  
• **问题在于 API 选择而非底层接口**：fwlr认为“随机整数”接口并非过低级，而是用户把“生成随机比特”和“按概率作选择”混为一谈。建议标准库提供`choice`等高级接口，直接从集合中均匀选取元素，并正确处理常见概率选择。  
• **关注随机性测试与白化**：westurner将讨论延伸到随机性检测，询问NIST SP 800-22等测试方案，并提到可通过白化变换改善分布的均匀性或正态性。

补充讨论：争议焦点是随机偏差是否足以影响实际应用，以及应由调用者自行正确处理，还是由标准库提供更安全、易用的抽象。

49983404.article_content:
There is a common pattern you see pop up in codebases everywhere that many of
us have written: given a set of objects, pick one at random. Every object should
have the same chance of being picked. A rather simple and direct solution is to
pick a big random number, then clamp that number to the number of choices by
modulo:
Set
<
T
> choices
=
ten_things
();
u64
r
=
random_u64
();
// uniform chance over [0..UINT64_MAX]
T
chosen
=
choices[r
%
10
];
I fondly remember choosing this option several times when I was much younger,
especially when writing C â its standard library does not offer anything
beyond
rand()
â and also my other language de jour, Haskell. After all,
it is a fairly immediate and intuitive solution when you have such a problem,
and almost any codebase or language, no matter how austere or feeble, will have
some
mechanism to pick a random number.
But there is a hidden problem with this solution: it doesnât preserve the
underlying uniform distribution of the given
random_u64()
function. That means
that the variability of the
chosen
object you pick doesnât respect what we
might intuitively think: we might think every item has a
1/10
chance of being
chosen. It does not.
(Non-)Preservation of uniform choice
Letâs start with a simpler problem: pick an integer from the interval
[0, 9]
. There are 10 possible picks. Assuming that our random choice function has
a
uniform distribution
, every integer will have a chance of
1/10 = 10%
of
being chosen.
Then, let us use that integer to randomly pick a value from a set of 3 objects,
using the modulo operator like above. The intuitive (implicit) hope is that this
operation picks one of the 3 objects, each with a
1/3 = 33.3%
chance; in other
words, we we want the resulting probability distribution to ârespectâ the
uniform distribution of the input variable.
Unfortunately, this is not the case; simply tabulating the outcomes makes that
obvious:
Input value  -> Choice
-----------------------------
{0, 3, 6, 9} -> choose object #1
{1, 4, 7}    -> choose object #2
{2, 5, 8}    -> choose object #3
In other words: of the given 10 inputs, 4 of them yield choice 1, while choice
2 and 3 only have 3 inputs that do so. This means choice 1 is picked 40% of the
time rather than the intended 33%, and likewise 2 and 3 are only picked 30% of
the time.
Itâs one of the classic blunders, especially when
random_u64()
is all
you have. Now, the correct behavior instead is a
random_between(l, h)
function which gives each inclusive number between
l
and
h
a
1/((h-l)+1)
chance of being picked. Such a function is, as we might now expect,
a bit more
complex
!
The issue in my mind is twofold. One, I think it is suboptimal API design to
only offer a uniform random function, especially given that one of its most
useful variants is easy to implement incorrectly. But it is also a good example
of mentally working in the wrong domain in the first place.
Giving an explicit distribution is (hopefully) easier
I think the first thing is the fact that an API like
random_u64()
is a bit
too
low level and specialized. We donât
really
want to sample a uniform
number but a more general operator to express âhow often does something happenâ.
On one hand, you rarely need to
only
pick a random number, you normally want
to pick some
object
out of some possible choices; second, it often is useful
to weigh certain objects as more or less likely than other objects â the
uniform distribution is not the only valuable one!
random_u64()
does not help
with either of these things; a
random_between(0, 9)
only helps with the first
at a glance (more on that shortly).
Most of the time, I think it is useful to instead reach for a more general
operator, that makes you confront these issues directly: a
random_choice()
function that takes a set of discrete options and their probability of being
chosen. In other words, you should spell out the probability distribution
yourself. With this, you can represent both of the previous behaviors, and many
more interesting ones.
Typically when we talk about probabilities we think of them as summing to
1.0
,
like the following reformulation of the original example; in such a design the
erroneous âlopsidedâ pick is going to stick out like a sore thumb:
T chosen = random_choice([
(First,  0.4), // 40% chance?!?!?!
(Second, 0.3), // 30% chance
(Third,  0.3), // 30% chance
])
I think this is a case (one of many) where a generalized API, a more abstract
API, can in fact make much of your code easier to reason about and write
correctly too. You should of course still have
random_u64()
and
random_between()
as well â but I think
random_choice()
is the
much better default tool because it will help you
fall into the pit of
success
.
Improving the API: relative integer weights
The previous interface is pedagogically nice but floating point instability can
muddle with our ability to pick the precise weights we might need, as they must
sum exactly to

data.title: Utah to let AI examine patients and prescribe medication without human oversight
data.author: healsdata
data.article_summary: 美国犹他州启动一项试点，允许医疗初创公司Nolla Health通过AI分析用户面部和病史，为轻中度痤疮诊断并开具八种外用药，逐步减少医生审核，未来或实现全自动。项目为期一年，月费4.99美元。尽管风险较低，AI医疗建议曾出现严重错误，引发对安全与监管的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕犹他州暂时允许 Nolla Health 以AI分析皮肤并开具痤疮药物，讨论其医疗价值、监管边界、安全性与责任归属。

不同观点：
• 支持试点者认为，痤疮属于低风险、主要依靠视觉判断且治疗方案成熟的领域；若助理医师进行20分钟远程问诊已足够，AI也可能胜任。它可减少预约、保险和候诊成本，提升医疗可及性，尤其适用于维A酸等常见药物。
• 更广泛的改革观点认为，许多处方药只是OTC药物的加强版，统一要求医生处方造成低效；对低风险疾病可逐步放宽限制，避免患者因繁琐流程而放弃治疗。
• 谨慎支持者赞成“先试点、后扩展”：前100例人工审核，之后由医生定期回顾，再抽查至少10%，以低风险场景检验并改进系统。
• 反对者质疑实际增益：若医生监督确有必要，AI可能增加误诊风险；若无需监督，药物就不应设为处方药。也有人主张禁止AI用于任何医疗场景，担忧模型错误及患者无法识别其局限。

补充讨论：争议核心是效率与可及性是否值得承担安全风险；标题被指夸大，犹他州并非全面允许“无人工介入”医疗，而是对该公司临时放行。评论还追问出错后的责任主体，并担心AI被滥用于索取强效药物。

49981197.article_content:
Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years.
TechSpot means tech analysis and advice
you can trust
.
A hot potato:
Being a doctor is one of the jobs expected to be least at risk from AI replacement. But a new program launched in Utah is raising questions over that assumption. A healthcare startup will begin offering AI examinations and prescriptions to patients without direct human oversight, making Utah the first state to replace a doctor with an AI.
The good news is that the program is currently very limited in its scope. It's just one year long and only for patients with mild-to-moderate acne.
The process works when a person signs up for Nolla Health's $4.99-per-month app and uses it to scan their face. After completing a medical history and personal information form, the AI analyzes their skin, identifies the acne problem, rates the skin's oiliness, and then generates a numerical acne severity score that ranges between clear skin and severe acne, reports
Bloomberg
.
The AI then combines that score with the provided medical information to recommend medication from a list of eight approved treatments.
While the program will eventually become fully automated, the first 100 prescriptions will have to be reviewed by actual doctors before they are submitted to the pharmacy.
In the second phase, the next 400 patients will have their prescriptions submitted to pharmacies by the AI and reviewed retrospectively by a physician weekly.
The final phase will involve a doctor reviewing at least 10% of the total prescriptions issued once a month.
We've repeatedly seen the dangers of putting your trust in AI when it comes to medical/healthcare advice. One of the more famous cases came last year when a 60-year-old man took ChatGPT's advice and replaced the salt in his diet with sodium bromide,
causing bromism
, a psychiatric disorder not commonly seen since the 19th century.
// Related Stories
Stanford researchers say the brain is actually two organs pretending to be one
Utah just became the first state to target VPN users for age verification
In March, Google
quietly dropped
an AI-powered search feature called What People Suggest, which offered crowdsourced health advice from people who share similar medical conditions or experiences. The move came just a couple of months after the company
removed several
of its AI Overviews following a report that found inaccurate information was being shown to users, potentially putting their health at risk.
In the case of Nolla Health, CEO Luis Wenus said the adverse effects of the eight approved medications are limited to localized skin irritation or dryness. The prescriptions are also limited to topical medications rather than pills.
While this is a small program, it could be the very first step toward AI taking the place of doctors, or at least being used to treat less serious conditions in patients.

data.title: Paramount Skydance has completed its $111B merger with Warner Bros. Discovery
data.author: Mgtyalx
data.article_summary: 派拉蒙旗下Skydance完成对华纳兄弟探索公司的1110亿美元合并，成立新公司Skydance，整合Paramount+、HBO Max、CBS、CNN及多项体育和影视资产。美国最高法院大法官卡根拒绝阻止交易。尽管多州曾以反垄断和竞争受损起诉，最终通过和解获批，包括保障电影投资发行及有线频道独立谈判，并设立CBS News和CNN编辑独立委员会。合并后公司负债约800亿美元，面临发展流媒体、维持现金流和改善电影业务的压力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕派拉蒙/天空之舞与华纳相关媒体整合的垄断风险、政治影响、商业前景及好莱坞衰落展开讨论。

不同观点：
• 反垄断担忧：合并会减少竞争、集中高预算影视与新闻资源，可能导致涨价、裁员；有人讽刺消费者得到的是“更少竞争”，并追问未来能否认定为反垄断并拆分。  
• 政治与媒体独立：部分评论者担心亲右翼或亲以色列资本获得CNN、娱乐及新闻的编辑影响力，CNN可能进一步“福克斯化”；也有人认为这是“前独裁时期”信号。相关观点存在对所有权背景及其影响的争议。  
• 商业前景悲观：华纳自1990年以来多次易主（Time、AOL、AT&T、Discovery等）均不理想，且新合并背负巨额债务；有人预测2030年前还会换东家。YouTube美国电视观看份额约13%，而派拉蒙/华纳合计约6%，显示其竞争力有限。  
• 相对乐观或淡然：娱乐选择比过去更多，类似合并未必成功；也有人认为自己本就不关注两家公司，合并后兴趣更低。  
• 行业结构危机：评论认为流媒体以少量剧集、短期利润取代传统长期制作体系，造成产量下降、裁员和人才外流；税收优惠、住房成本又削弱洛杉矶生态，行业日益被“关系户”主导。  
• 文化消费抵抗：有人主张减少消费，以降低媒体巨头的需求和影响力。

补充讨论：David Ellison被讽刺为“靠出身成功”，其从演员梦转向右翼媒体资本的经历被视为好莱坞衰落的象征。

Paramount Skydance completed its $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery today, after a last-ditch effort to block the deal was rejected by Supreme Court Justice Elena Kagan.
The post-merger company is called Skydance, taking the name of a firm that Paramount bought in a separate deal last year. The new Skydance combines two of the largest movie studios, streaming services Paramount+ and HBO Max, CBS, CNN, “and a portfolio of live sports including CBS Sports and TNT Sports, as well as a deep programming library and expansive collection of brands and franchises,” Skydance said today in a
press release
announcing completion of the deal.
The merger was delayed a bit by a lawsuit filed by California and 11 other states. In July, US District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in the Northern District of California
ruled
that the combination would likely reduce competition substantially and violate antitrust laws.
California settled the lawsuit
last month, and the other states involved went along with the compromise. A coalition of free speech and media advocacy groups
urged the judge
to reject the settlement, saying it will give residents of the states that sued Paramount “virtually nothing.”
Martínez-Olguín
approved
the settlement on September 30, saying the deal “represents a reasonable factual and legal resolution of the dispute.” She wrote that a typical settlement “does not fully remediate an alleged violation or even necessarily resolve the ultimate factual and legal issues of a case.” It “reflects a compromise of the claims short of full adjudication—compromise that may leave some dissatisfaction for both sides and the public but a compromise that saves the risk, time, and expense of litigating through trial.”
The settlement addresses the lawsuit’s complaints about film distribution “by requiring certain minimum thresholds of investment and release of domestic films,” and addresses complaints about licensing of basic cable channels with “requirements for continued, separate negotiations of distribution for the two entities’ basic cable holdings,” the judge wrote. Objections based on “hopes and desires for the proposed consent decree to reach farther—to achieve more—do not rise to the level of legal violations upon which the Court can reject the parties’ negotiated resolution,” she wrote.
Merger opponents strike out at Supreme Court
A separate lawsuit in the same district court, filed by five consumers who purchase streaming service subscriptions or other video products, also failed. The five consumers sought review in the US Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, which rejected the plaintiffs’ request. The plaintiffs then filed an
emergency application
to block the deal with Kagan, who handles emergency requests for the Ninth Circuit. Kagan
denied
the application yesterday without comment.
The settlement with California requires Skydance to set up an “Editorial Independence Board” for CBS News and CNN. The board’s members would be chosen by Skydance and report to the company’s board of directors. The settlement term was adopted amid concerns about CBS and CNN’s ability to report news independently. CNN CEO Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss will
retain their roles
in the merged firm.
Paramount CEO David Ellison
reportedly
told Trump administration officials that he would make big changes at CNN, a frequent target of Trump’s wrath. Last year, Paramount won US approval to buy Skydance
after reaching a $16 million settlement
with Trump and agreeing to install what Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr described as a “
bias monitor
” at CBS.
The US Department of Justice
approved
the Paramount/Warner merger in June, a decision that reportedly surprised DOJ staff lawyers who were leaning toward recommending that the agency file an antitrust lawsuit to block it. In September, the FCC
allowed Paramount
to finance the merger by selling large equity stakes to the sovereign wealth funds of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Qatar.
Reuters reports
that Skydance is “expected to carry about $80 billion in debt, putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance.” The sovereign wealth funds have non-voting shares in Skydance, while the Ellison family and RedBird Capital Partners own 100 percent of the voting shares.

• 反垄断担忧：合并会减少竞争、集中高预算影视与新闻资源，可能导致涨价、裁员；有人讽刺消费者得到的是“更少竞争”，并追问未来能否认定为反垄断并拆分。  
• 政治与媒体独立：部分评论者担心亲右翼或亲以色列资本获得CNN、娱乐及新闻的编辑影响力，CNN可能进一步“福克斯化”；也有人认为这是“前独裁时期”信号。相关观点存在对所有权背景及其影响的争议。  
• 商业前景悲观：华纳自1990年以来多次易主（Time、AOL、AT&T、Discovery等）均不理想，且新合并背负巨额债务；有人预测2030年前还会换东家。YouTube美国电视观看份额约13%，而派拉蒙/华纳合计约6%，显示其竞争力有限。  
• 相对乐观或淡然：娱乐选择比过去更多，类似合并未必成功；也有人认为自己本就不关注两家公司，合并后兴趣更低。  
• 行业结构危机：评论认为流媒体以少量剧集、短期利润取代传统长期制作体系，造成产量下降、裁员和人才外流；税收优惠、住房成本又削弱洛杉矶生态，行业日益被“关系户”主导。  
• 文化消费抵抗：有人主张减少消费，以降低媒体巨头的需求和影响力。

补充讨论：David Ellison被讽刺为“靠出身成功”，其从演员梦转向右翼媒体资本的经历被视为好莱坞衰落的象征。

data.title: LLMs may have helped my RSI
data.author: vaughands
data.article_summary: 作者长期因打字、编程和弹琴患重复性劳损，尤其频繁操作特殊键和复杂组合键会导致前臂灼痛。2026年起，借助LLM代理完成大量机械编码，减少长时间、高强度键盘操作，转而更多撰写设计文档和审查代码。尽管产出更多，手臂疼痛却明显减轻，作者认为LLM可能改善了其健康状况。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕重复性劳损（RSI）的缓解与预防，讨论输入方式、人体工学、工作习惯，以及语音和AI工具对健康的影响。

不同观点：
• 语音输入派：推荐 Talon、Cursorless、voxtype 等工具，以语音代替键盘操作，减少手臂和拇指负担；即使尚未患RSI，也可在手臂疲劳时使用。  
• 人体工学与习惯派：减少鼠标使用、改用人体工学键盘、改善打字姿势和技巧，并将显示器顶部调至与眼睛平齐；通过先在脑中构建程序模型、减少反复试错来降低击键量。  
• 键盘布局派：有人认为改用Dvorak布局后RSI消失并长期未复发，同时在不同布局间切换可能进一步减轻负担。  
• 工作方式变化派：从整日写代码转向写更多 prose、或职业发展后打字减少，可能缓解症状，但当事人也承认难以确定因果。  
• AI影响存在分歧：有人认为语音和AI能减少输入、保护手部与视力；但也有人指出，实际使用AI反而带来更多打字。

补充讨论：评论还提到应在疼痛恶化前进行预防性训练，并推荐相关健康读物；“递归自我改进”和系鞋带的说法带有明显玩笑或讽刺意味，焦点在于“技术是否真正减少劳动和伤害”。

49973644.article_content:
October 05, 2026
Posts
LLMs may have immensely helped my RSI
I was playing piano for the first time in a while the other day and noticed: I didn’t feel any RSI. Maybe a bit and some tenderness, but not much at all. And no, I don’t mean
recursive self improvement
that is so trendy and topical right now. You see, for many years (starting as early as 2017) I had suffered some form of repetitive strain injury from as far as my doctors and I could tell was from simply typing on a keyboard and using my keyboard simply too much. I was learning to play piano, as you can imagine from the prior passage. This all added up to quite the strain on my arms at the end of the day. There has been good periods and bad periods since that time, but I remember coming home some days and my forearms would just be absolutely
burning
. The pain is the sort that you don’t forget. You experience it and never forget. I even read books such as
“The Mindbody Prescription: Healing the Body, Healing the Pain”
to try and reduce this. You don’t start reading books for treating your pain; you grasp at them because you’re desperate.
I learned through the years to manage this, exercise more and take more breaks. I had gotten the pain down to some periods of 0-2 a month at most and tried all the usual stuff: ergonomic keyboards, more breaks, less time at a keyboard and various other techniques. Many of these things helped a lot but going a full day could be quite the task if it was a particularly heavy day. I also learned to type on home row retraining years of bad habits when I realized the some of the strain was coming from moving my wrist all over the keyboard and not keeping things straight. So, all this to say that I came a long way from the weekly pain that I would be experiencing that was quite a burning feeling.
But the most noticeable days of pain had something in common: the types of keys I would be striking. You see, I would be able to type 20 pages of a design document with some rest in-between and not feel much at all. Sure, I might have some soreness from striking the keys (and still do, after writing a post like this one I may need some small breaks in between if not using voice dictation). But this was nothing compared to the days where I would write code for 4-5 hours in a stretch. This was even more common when I was a junior. This would normally involve trying to type special characters all over the keyboard. Hitting angled brackets, hitting various FN keys, striking home, end, tons of modifier keys, contorting my wrist in all sorts of ways that I really should not be. This was part of the motivation to learn to type “the right way”: to reduce these types of problems. Probably something that made it worse is that my hands are much smaller than average as a male. My finger span could barely reach an octave if I tried and much more than this is tough:
So, yeah. Small hands. I had similar problems raiding in
Final Fantasy XIV
and never really thought about it much until I started talking with some of my raid members and realized they were using combos that would involve Ctrl and up to the number 5! I cannot make that reach without some serious stretching that you can
definitely
feel.
Something changed slowly in 2026 though. I still write quite a bit of code by hand when it’s called for and needed. But increasingly, more code is being written by agents. When I want to do small refactors that are mechanical, I simply ask for then. An entire feature that I might write out in the afternoon which could span 4 - 5 hours of typing and debugging are replaced with prompts and maybe 30 minutes of manual refinement.
I spend more time writing good design specifications and reviewing that of others. I review more code, but I am typing more on home row as a result. I might actually write more character per character than I used to but I am spending less time all over the keyboard and more time just typing… English prose. All that fits in the span of my fingertips. It is also probably true that I spent more time in meetings which is a natural consequence of becoming more senior. But to be clear: I shipped more code this year probably than any other year before it (I’m working on a greenfield product, working in Healthcare prior it was a different story).
I woke the other day thinking: hmm, I’ve not felt some arm pain in any serious capacity in quite some time. That’s interesting. I’ve felt some fatigue, sure. I mentioned that in my recent post talking about my new
Macbook Air here
. But serious, burning pain? It’s been quite some time! Perhaps it could be because I simply spend more time writing essays rather than moving my hands all over a keyboard pecking at keys.
I have my own set of complicated feelings of LLMs (gone are the bouts of satisfaction I would get hammering out code in an afternoon and watching it work at the end of the day). However, it seems increasingly more likely that from a health perspective perhaps they have been a boon t

Why Query Rewriting Matters for Dataflow
Most databases work the same way: a query arrives, the engine builds an execution plan, scans tables, joins rows, filters, aggregates, and returns the result. Every time the query runs, the work repeats from scratch. This pull-based model has served relational databases for decades, but it carries an inherent cost: read latency is proportional to the complexity of the query and the size of the data it touches.
Readyset takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of re-executing queries on demand, Readyset compiles each query into a
dataflow graph
— a network of operators (joins, filters, aggregations, projections) that continuously maintains the query's result as the underlying data changes. When a row is inserted, updated, or deleted in the upstream database, the change propagates through the graph, and the cached result is incrementally updated. Reads become lookups into a pre-computed materialized view, not full query executions.
This is the key difference: traditional engines optimize
how
to execute a query each time it runs. Readyset optimizes
once
, at cache-creation time, and then maintains the result incrementally forever. The tradeoff is that the query must be expressed in a form the dataflow engine can compile — and that form is more restrictive than what SQL allows.
What the Dataflow Engine Requires
SQL is a declarative language. The same logical query can be written in many equivalent ways: correlated subqueries, derived tables,
CTEs
,
LATERAL
joins, nested aggregations. A traditional optimizer treats these as interchangeable representations and picks the best execution plan regardless of syntax.
Readyset's dataflow compiler is not a traditional optimizer. It translates SQL into a directed acyclic graph of streaming operators, where each operator receives changes from its inputs and emits changes to its outputs. This architecture imposes structural constraints that SQL syntax doesn't:
Binary joins with equality predicates.
Each join in the dataflow graph connects exactly two inputs via column-equality predicates (
a.id = b.id
). The engine uses these equalities to maintain hash-based join state. Range predicates, expression-based join keys, or multi-table
ON
conditions are not directly supported.
No correlated execution.
In a traditional engine, a correlated subquery runs once per outer row — a nested-loop pattern. The dataflow graph has no concept of "per outer row." Every operator sees the full stream of changes from its inputs. Correlated subqueries must be rewritten into equivalent joins that the dataflow can maintain incrementally.
Flat join structure preferred.
Derived tables (subqueries in
FROM
) are supported by the dataflow engine, but with a cost: a derived table compiles into a fully materialized intermediate node that cannot be parameterized. Every distinct combination of input data produces a stored result, regardless of whether the outer query needs it. Inlining the derived table — absorbing its
FROM
items,
WHERE
filters, and projections into the outer query — eliminates this intermediate materialization and lets the engine build parameterized lookups directly against the base tables. The rewrite pipeline aggressively inlines derived tables where semantically safe, reserving the materialized form for cases where inlining would change the query's meaning.
Supported join types.
The engine supports
INNER JOIN
,
LEFT OUTER JOIN
, and
CROSS JOIN
.
RIGHT JOIN
and
FULL OUTER JOIN
are not supported because their incremental maintenance in a streaming context requires tracking absence of matches on both sides — a significantly harder problem.
Aggregation boundaries.
GROUP BY
and aggregate functions (
COUNT
,
SUM
, etc.) compile into stateful operators that maintain running totals. The engine requires that each aggregated query projects at least one aggregate-derived expression, and that
GROUP BY
keys are explicit column references (not positional numbers or aliases).
These constraints mean that a syntactically valid SQL query — one that PostgreSQL or MySQL would execute without complaint — may not be directly compilable by Readyset, or may compile into a less efficient dataflow graph than necessary. The query rewrite pipeline exists to bridge this gap.

data.title: How Fast is Python 3.15?
data.author: Qem
data.article_summary: 文章通过递归斐波那契和冒泡排序两类程序，测试 Python 3.10—3.15 的单线程、多线程性能，并对比 JIT、免费线程、PyPy、Node.js 和 Rust。结果显示，Python 3.15 相比 3.14 提升有限；PyPy 在递归计算中约快5.5倍，Node.js略逊，Rust则大幅领先。作者强调该测试仅供参考，不能代表全部场景。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕 Python 3.15 性能改进的基准测试、测试方法及进一步优化方案展开讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持性能评测但强调局限**：makaimc认为，Python公开发布35年来仍有较大性能提升空间；相关测试可作为了解3.15进展的快速参考，但无法代表编程语言“客观且普遍”的性能。
• **质疑基准覆盖面**：rurban指出仅使用两个基准测试，覆盖范围过窄，难以支撑广泛结论。
• **质疑统计精度**：bjourne认为，若每个测试只运行三次并取算术平均，不应报告过多小数位；同时建议性能测试使用几何平均数，因为它通常比算术平均更合适。
• **主张通过代码迁移获得性能**：brianwawok认为，与其等待 Python 本身变快，不如借助 Claude 将 Python 代码转换为 Rust 或 Go，可能获得约10倍加速。
• **提出算法级优化**：DroneBetter建议为 Fibonacci 增加基于“平方求幂”的快速算法，并可对现有函数使用`functools.cache`；还提到将多项式编码为整数等方法，强调这类方案主要增加算术计算、减少控制流。
• **指出其他工具更快**：actionfromafar认为，现有测试结果仍不如 Shed Skin。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 Python 性能提升应依靠解释器/版本优化，还是算法改进、编译到其他语言；同时，基准数量、统计方法和结果精度也影响结论可信度。

49984652.article_content:
How fast is Python 3.15?
Posted by
on
2026-10-05T10:13:17Z
under
It's October once again, and that means it is time to take the new release of Python for a spin (technically, it is the 3.15.0rc3 release that I'm using, the official 3.15 release is still a few days out). As I did with my
Python 3.14 performance
article of a year ago, today I'm sharing a new run of my informal Python benchmark, comparing Python 3.15 against previous interpreters all the way back to 3.10.
If you are not interested in the charts and the tables and just want to read my analysis, feel free to jump to the
conclusions
section at the end.
The benchmark
I just called my benchmark "informal". What does that mean?
Getting an objective and universal measure of the performance of a programming language is impossible. All you can do is write some programs and run them to get a measure of their performance. Other programs may show similar performance characteristics or they may not, there is really no way to know. My intention with this benchmark is just to get a feel for the performance changes across versions of Python, but I want to make it clear that I'm not trying to obtain a comprehensive performance profile of the Python interpreter.
For my benchmark I will be running two programs called
fibo.py
and
bubble.py
, which
you can inspect
if you like. These are the same programs I used in past editions of this benchmark. The first calculates numbers from the
Fibonacci sequence
, and the second sorts numbers using the
bubble sort
algorithm.
I've chosen these two programs as representative of two classes of algorithms. The Fibonacci calculation is done using
recursion
, which I have found to be somewhat inefficient in Python interpreters. On the other side, the bubble sort only uses for-loops, without any recursion. There are other types of programs that my benchmark does not attempt to cover. In particular, note that I'm not including
I/O bound
code in this benchmark.
Because some of the performance improvements in recent Python versions revolve around multi-threading, I also created a multi-threaded variation for each program, so in total I have four different tests.
The testing matrix
The complete testing matrix is actually fairly complex, because I have to run the four program variations under all the Python versions, plus the JIT and free-threading alternatives for those that have them. I like to run the tests under PyPy as well, because this interpreter has shown impressive performance in past runs of this benchmark. And to place Python performance within the wider ecosystem, I've also ported the two programs to JavaScript (Node.js) and Rust.
Here is the full test matrix that I've worked with:
2 test scripts
fibo.py
: calculates Fibonacci numbers, with recursion
bubble.py
: sorts a list of randomly generated numbers, without recursion
2 threading modes
Single-threaded
4 parallel threads
6 Python versions, plus recent versions of PyPy, Node.js and Rust:
CPython
3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, 3.15
PyPy
3.12
Node

3 Python interpreters
Standard
Just-In-Time (JIT): only for CPython 3.13+
Free-threading (FT): only for CPython 3.13+
Readers of my previous benchmarks may recall that I had an additional dimension in my matrix for Linux vs. macOS. Given that there were no significant differences between them in the two previous runs of the benchmark, I've decided to drop the macOS tests this time around, so all tests were executed on my Linux laptop, which has an Intel Core i5 CPU and runs Gentoo Linux.
The method I'm using to measure the performance of each participant in this benchmark is to run the test program three times and take the average duration of the three. In the tables of results that I share below I also show the speed difference versus the 3.15 version, and when it makes sense also the speed difference versus the previous version of a given interpreter. For speed comparisons I'm using a simple ratio, where 1x means same speed, 0.5x means half speed (or that it took twice the time to run), 2x means twice as fast (or that it ran in half the time if you prefer), etc. Hopefully this makes sense.
Test 1: fibo.py, single-threaded

• **提出算法级优化**：DroneBetter建议为 Fibonacci 增加基于“平方求幂”的快速算法，并可对现有函数使用`functools.cache`；还提到将多项式编码为整数等方法，强调这类方案主要增加算术计算、减少控制流。
• **指出其他工具更快**：actionfromafar认为，现有测试结果仍不如 Shed Skin。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于 Python 性能提升应依靠解释器/版本优化，还是算法改进、编译到其他语言；同时，基准数量、统计方法和结果精度也影响结论可信度。

49977531.article_content:
What’s Earth’s dominant species by mass?
You might have heard that all the ants in the world weigh as much combined as all the humans. That isn’t true. We outweigh ants 5 to 1.
1
Termites might have us beat, though.
2
Either way, it’s not really a fair comparison. There are thousands of species of ants and termites, and just one species of human.
But if we’re judging each species based on how much total mass they have – that is, by its “biomass” – who actually comes out on top? Turns out there are some surprising winners.
Antarctic Krill: 379 million tonnes
Let’s start with our division: animals. Humans are pretty close to the top for a single species, weighing in at about 350 million metric tons.
3
The top-placing wild species is Antarctic krill, with a 2009 estimate placing them at 379 million metric tons. Each individual krill weighs only about 2 grams or 0.07 ounces, but their sheer population in the Southern Ocean puts them in a statistical dead heat with us – and keeps gigantic blue whales comfortably fed.
But both humans and krill lag behind the true winner for animals: cattle. Cattle are easily the top domesticated animal species, with about 650 million metric tons of biomass. Pigs are in second, at about 140 million metric tons – placing them behind humans and krill.
Cattle: 650 million tonnes
Unfortunately for cattle, animals are almost the lightest of all the kingdoms of life. The most comprehensive study, (Bar-On et. al 2018) measures the different kingdoms by their carbon mass specifically. Carbon is only a portion of an organism, so this method gives smaller numbers. But those numbers are more meaningful for, say, tracking the flow of food energy through the biosphere (think of eating a pound of watermelon versus a pound of steak). For example, the 650 million tons of cattle on Earth represent only 61 million tons of carbon.
Animals as a whole have 2 billion tons of carbon. That means we handily outclass viruses (0.2 billion tons) but are beaten by protists (4 billion), archaea (7 billion), fungi (12 billion), bacteria (70 billion) and especially plants (450 billion).
Most of the world’s bacteria live in aquifers and seafloor sediments, which are hard to study. It’s possible that one extremely dominant undersea bacteria species has the world’s highest biomass, but more likely the winner will be a plant.
So what plant has the most biomass in the world? The winner for animals was a domesticated species, so let’s start with domesticated plants.
The first species that might come to mind are the major cereal grains like rice, wheat, and corn (maize). Of these, maize has the largest annual harvest by mass, totaling 1.1 billion tons – nearly double the mass of cattle. But the true biggest crop isn’t a grain at all.
That honor goes to sugar cane, with the harvest topping 2 billion metric tons in 2023.
4
So humanity harvests about 6 times our collective weight in sugar cane every year. Sugar cane is also a perennial, meaning that its root system persists between harvests. This means total mass of living sugar cane on average throughout the year is probably higher than an annual crop like maize.
Sugar cane: 2 billion tonnes
But there’s still one more subcategory to look at: wild plants. It’s time to take on the trees.
Trees seem to hold all the superlatives. The most massive individual organism comes from a tree species: Pando the clonal colony of aspen trees with interconnected roots which weighs 6,000 metric tons all on its own. But aspens are pretty rare. Is there a more common tree with more total mass as a species?
For that, we have to look to the largest forest in the world: the boreal forests that ring the arctic circle. In those forests, just 3 or 4 species can represent over half of the total mass of the forest. By contrast, tropical forests can require over a hundred species to reach the same mark.
5
Two candidates boreal trees came up in a search of the literature. One is the Black Spruce,
Picea mariana
, which is the most common tree in arctic Canada. According to Canada’s National Forest Inventory,
6
over 11 billion tons of black spruce are growing in the country, and some grow in the USA as well.
Black Spruce: More than 11 billion tonnes
The other candidate is the Dahurian Larch, the most common tree in Russia. Russia’s forest inventory doesn’t have as detailed numbers by species,
7
but larches as whole in Russia are about 35.6% of Russia’s forest land, and Russia has a total of 82.2 billion cubic meters of forest. From what I could find, there are 2 main species of larch in Russia: the Dahurian Larch in the East and the Siberian Larch in the west, and the Dahurian is the more common of the two so it must be at least 50% of the total. Calculating the numbers and using the density of larch wood, that gives 16.8 billion tons of larch in Russia, of which at least 8.4 billion tons (and possibly more) is Dahurian larch.
Dahurian Larch: At least 8.4 billion tonnes, maybe more

data.title: California closed the Montana license plate loophole
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 加州通过SB 1406，正式堵住富人用蒙大拿空壳公司注册豪车、规避销售税的漏洞。新法扩大“企业”定义，并规定只要股东、合伙人或受益所有人中有一名加州居民，企业及其车辆即被视为加州居民，须缴纳使用税；相关负责人还可能承担欠税、罚款及刑事责任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加州拟打击通过蒙大拿州牌照、外州 LLC 或经销商牌照规避车辆注册税费的做法，引发对税收公平、执法可行性及车辆管理制度的争论。

不同观点：
• 支持加强征税者认为，这是富人利用法律漏洞逃税，加州财政压力大，车辆应按实际居住和使用地纳税；也有人从环保角度支持限制高污染汽车文化。  
• 反对严厉立法者认为，相关公司可能是真实合法的 Montana LLC，并非“假公司”；仅因一名公司成员住在加州，就追征外州车辆税，可能违宪且难以证明车辆曾在加州使用。  
• 多人认为根本问题是各州标准割裂、注册和税费制度复杂。建议建立全国统一标准、通用牌照，或允许长期保留牌照，以减少搬迁、跨州出行和执法摩擦。  
• 有评论指出，加州经销商牌照、蒙大拿牌照可显著降低注册费和消费税；但实际跨州购车需证明居住地、运输出境并办理公证，未必容易规避。  
• 批评加州 DMV 的观点认为，其通过 PNO（计划不运营）等复杂规则持续收取费用、罚款和利息，核心目标是增加财政收入，而非服务车主。  
• 另一观点主张改用使用税，认为按实际使用征税更公平，也能减少套利。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“堵漏”与过度执法的界限，以及税收、环保、行政便利和个人财产权之间如何平衡。

Joe Sohm/Visions of America/Universal Images Group via Getty Images

It’s official: California has closed the
Montana license plate loophole
. After more than seven months of legislative shuffling, CA State Bill 1406 (“Sales and Use Tax Law: vehicles: shell companies”) became law on Sept. 30, 2026, making it much harder to get away with the shell-company shenanigans rich Californians have exploited for decades.
Existing California law says any vehicle, vessel, or aircraft a California resident “shipped or brought into the state” is subject to taxation under the state’s Sales and Use Tax Law, whether it is registered there or not. This same rule applied to vehicles registered to a business, but because businesses aren’t people, the law set different standards for establishing its “California-ness.”
Essentially, if more than half of your business was held outside California, you could keep your vehicle registered to that out-of-state business without paying Use Tax in California. This seems like a reasonable qualifier on paper. Say you live in Nevada and your vehicle is registered to your business based there; if you operate a branch office on the California side of Lake Tahoe, for instance, you could legally keep your car there on Nevada plates so long as the bulk of the business was based in Nevada. This is a gross oversimplification, but you get the basic idea.
Porsche edited by TD
This arrangement seemed to work just fine for everyone involved until a bunch of people started registering fake LLCs in Montana (though not exclusively), which doesn’t charge sales tax on vehicle purchases (or require owners to inspect/smog their cars). Under the old law, only companies and limited liability companies were subject to the California-ness test; the new law expands that definition to include partnerships, limited partnerships, and limited liability partnerships. And then there’s the whammy (emphasis mine).
“The bill would also provide that, for purposes of the above-described presumption,
a shell company, as defined, is a resident of this state if any shareholder, partner, member, or beneficial owner is a resident of this state
,” the
bill summary
says.
In other words, the old 50% test is out. If
anyone
running the business is a California resident (by the updated definition outlined above), then the whole business is a California resident, and any assets (including Lamborghinis and Bugattis) held in the state are subject to California taxation. And just in case you need it spelled out, that means you’re on the hook for that tax liability as a fellow partner/member:
“The bill would hold any officer, manager, partner, beneficial owner, or member of a shell company personally liable for any unpaid taxes, and any interest and penalties on those taxes,
the nonpayment of which may constitute a crime
, due on the purchase of a vehicle, vessel, or aircraft.”
Better make sure your paperwork is in order. The tax man’s a-comin’.

• 反对严厉立法者认为，相关公司可能是真实合法的 Montana LLC，并非“假公司”；仅因一名公司成员住在加州，就追征外州车辆税，可能违宪且难以证明车辆曾在加州使用。  
• 多人认为根本问题是各州标准割裂、注册和税费制度复杂。建议建立全国统一标准、通用牌照，或允许长期保留牌照，以减少搬迁、跨州出行和执法摩擦。  
• 有评论指出，加州经销商牌照、蒙大拿牌照可显著降低注册费和消费税；但实际跨州购车需证明居住地、运输出境并办理公证，未必容易规避。  
• 批评加州 DMV 的观点认为，其通过 PNO（计划不运营）等复杂规则持续收取费用、罚款和利息，核心目标是增加财政收入，而非服务车主。  
• 另一观点主张改用使用税，认为按实际使用征税更公平，也能减少套利。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“堵漏”与过度执法的界限，以及税收、环保、行政便利和个人财产权之间如何平衡。

Patrick Tomlinson and Niki Robinson awarded $575K US settlement from City of Milwaukee
Image  |  1000027449
Caption: Niki Robinson, left, and Patrick Tomlinson have been awarded a $575,000 US settlement by the City Milwaukee after armed police officers came to their home 55 times in two years responding to bogus reports of violent crime. (Submitted by Patrick Tomlinson)
Load image
The first time heavily armed police officers showed up at Patrick Tomlinson's house, he was asleep in bed, naked.
It was 1 a.m. on July 25, 2022, and someone had reported a hostage situation at his house in Milwaukee, where he lives with his wife, Niki Robinson.
"All of a sudden there's people pounding on the door," Tomlinson told
As It Happens
host Nil Kӧksal.
"I go outside to be pulled out of the house by eight or nine police officers [and] handcuffed on the front porch, which I can tell you is the least fun I've had handcuffed and naked in my life."
Tomlinson, a science fiction writer and comedian, hadn't committed a crime. He was the victim of "swatting," a harassment technique in which someone places a hoax call reporting a serious threat in order to send armed police to the target's home.
Over the course of the next two and a half years, Tomlinson and Robinson were swatted 55 times, despite repeatedly explaining their situation to the Milwaukee Police Department. They sued, and have been awarded a $575,000 US settlement from the City of Milwaukee.
LISTEN | Interview with 'swatting' victim Patrick Tomlinson:
Media Audio | As It Happens :
Caption: A Milwaukee couple was awarded a $575,000 US settlement from the city after armed police officers showed up at their homes 55 times in two years responding to bogus reports of violent crimes. Patrick Tomlinson speaks to As It Happens host Nil Kӧksal about suffering years of targeted harassment.
Open full embed in new tab
(external link)

When asked for comment, Milwaukee police referred CBC to city attorney Evan Goyke, who did not respond to multiple requests for comment.
“While Niki and Patrick’s settlement provided closure and an acknowledgment of the violations of their rights, it is just as important that Milwaukee be more proactive looking forward," Jack Idlas, a lawyer for the couple, said in an emailed statement.
"The city has made no changes to policy and no officers have been disciplined for violating Niki and Patrick’s constitutional rights. That’s hard to believe after the taxpayers settled for over a half million dollars.
It started with a tweet
Tomlinson traces his troubles back to a social media post he made seven years ago about Canadian comedian Norm Macdonald.
In September 2018, he wrote on Twitter, now X: “Hot take: I’ve never found Norm Macdonald funny and was pretty sure all my comedy friends who did were either nuts or screwing with me."
After that, he says, he experienced years of online harassment, which is
described in detail in an article in the Independent
(external link)
. That harassment, he says, eventually escalated into swatting.
"Our stalkers had specifically told us that they were going to begin swatting us…. We spoke to a dispatcher. We spoke with a desk sergeant. And both of them said there's nothing we can do," he said.
"Two weeks later, here I am, you know, on my front porch in the middle of the night, exposed to all my neighbours with shotguns and pistols and AR-15s pointed at my head."

Police were aware that Tomlinson's home was the target of swatting calls, according to internal memos and emails submitted as court evidence in the lawsuit.
On Aug. 3, 2022, one officer sent a memo to the acting police captain requesting the couple's home be marked as a "swatter house." The captain declined, saying it could cause a "complacency issue for responding officers.”
In bodycam footage from one incident, shared with CBC by Tomlinson's lawyers, an officer can be heard saying: "This guy keeps getting swatted."
Nevertheless, Tomlinson says, the police kept showing up, sometimes multiple times per day.
On one occasion, an officer entered his home without permission, according to an agreed statement of facts filed in connection with the lawsuit. On several occasions, officers searched the couple's home without a warrant.
Tomlinson says some of the officers responding to the hoax calls were "professional and sympathetic."
"Others, much less so," he said.

data.title: Ask HN: Why is Ask HN only showing me 14 posts?
data.author: Gooblebrai
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hacker News 的 Ask HN 页面显示的帖子数量减少、内容异常，究竟是正常筛选机制、界面故障还是用户端问题。

不同观点：
• [dang] 澄清讨论对象是 `/ask` 而非首页：由于 `/asknew` 或 `/newest` 中的帖子没有获得足够赞数，未达到进入 `/ask` 的门槛，因此页面可能出现空缺。可考虑用新帖填补，但筛选方式尚不明确。  
• [ThrowawayR2] 认为 `/ask` 本来就是经过筛选的列表；若想查看未筛选的全部内容，应访问 `/asknew`。  
• [altairprime] 认为页面可能显示了非 Ask 内容，属于网站故障，建议通过页脚 Contact 联系管理员。  
• [kencausey] 不确定 Ask HN 是否应显示更多帖子，但也建议向 hn@ycombinator.com 反馈。  
• [bigwheels]、[Aboutplants]、[aktenlage]、[tonymet] 等观察到页面只有 15 条，且过去似乎有分页；[dmitrygr] 则表示自己看到的是通常的 30 条，说明问题可能并非所有用户都能复现。  
• [tcfhgj] 提出可能是浏览器插件或脚本（如“无 AI 版 HN”）导致显示异常。  
• [lurker919]、[gj0] 将其视为罕见的 HN 前端或部署 bug，后者讽刺可能是未经审查的自动生成代码导致。

补充讨论：争议焦点在于“15 条是否为设计上的筛选结果，还是实际故障”；现有评论同时提供了服务端筛选、用户端插件和网站 bug 三种解释，但缺乏统一结论。

data.title: OpenSSH 10.6
data.author: torcete
data.article_summary: OpenSSH 10.6（2026-10-06）发布，包含多项安全修复和功能改进：加强SFTP路径校验、修复GSSAPI凭据处理问题，并禁用LZ77字典压缩以缓解跨通道侧信道攻击。命令行用户名限制反斜杠和美元符号。scp的-R选项开始弃用，部分老旧平台支持也将移除。因近期安全报告增多，项目将更频繁发布版本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenSSH 新版本的安全修复、漏洞响应机制、平台兼容性及项目维护。

不同观点：
• **安全加固受到肯定**：重点修复“Crossing the Streams”压缩侧信道问题。该漏洞类似 CRIME，利用不同会话共享 LZ77 状态，可能泄露信息；评论者也欢迎安全修复发布速度加快。  
• **更积极的发布策略**：OpenSSH 团队指出，AI 工具发现的安全漏洞常被其他研究者独立发现，意味着未公开报告的漏洞可能被攻击者利用，因此将更频繁发布版本，尽快让用户获得修复。有人认为这比 curl 对待 AI 报告的方式更健康，但也理解双方立场。  
• **维护响应获得高度评价**：用户分享非安全性的 QoS bug 经报告后一天内就获得测试版本、修复确认及目标发行版信息，称赞 Damien 和团队的响应效率。  
• **平台兼容性担忧**：OS X SDK 27 及以上移除了 OpenSSH 依赖的沙箱 API，暂时没有明显替代方案，导致 sshd 无法继续使用相关沙箱机制。  
• **项目资源问题**：有人关注 OpenSSH 的捐赠渠道及资金状况，间接引出核心开源基础设施的长期维护经费问题。

补充讨论：争议主要集中在如何处理 AI 发现的漏洞及发布节奏；评论总体支持更快修复，但也承认不同项目采取不同策略各有合理性。

OpenSSH: Release Notes
Open
SSH
Release Notes
OpenSSH 10.6
/
10.6p1
(2026-10-06)
OpenSSH 10.6 was released on 2026-10-06. It is available from the
mirrors listed at
https://www.openssh.com/
.
OpenSSH is a 100% complete SSH protocol 2.0 implementation and
includes sftp client and server support.
Recently the OpenSSH team have received a large number of security
bug reports, many of which are findings from AI models or made with
AI assistance. While many AI reports are determined not to have
security impact when considered in the context of a realistic
threat model, we very much welcome these reports, especially when
combined with human triage, analysis, test-cases and particularly
when accompanied by proposed fixes.
** We have seen a number of cases where a security bug identified
** by AI tools is subsequently independently discovered by a
** different researcher. This suggests that adversaries who do not
** report bugs to OSS projects are likely to be able to discover
** these bugs too. Given this, the OpenSSH team will, for now, be
** making more frequent releases to get bugfixes into users' hands
** more quickly rather than batching them until the next planned
** release.
Once again, we would like to thank the OpenSSH community for their
continued support of the project, especially those who contributed
code or patches, reported bugs, tested snapshots or donated to the
project. More information on donations may be found at:
https://www.openssh.com/donations.html
Future deprecation notice
-------------------------
*
scp(1)
: begin deprecating the -R flag, which is used to perform a
remote-to-remote copy by executing scp on a remote host. This
option is a fragile optimisation that is difficult to use because
it requires credentials on the remote host. It also creates
security risks if the shell quoting rules on the remote system
where the copy is performed differ from the client's expectations.
From OpenSSH 10.6, this option will continue to work but will
cause a deprecation warning to be emitted to standard error. In
a future release, the option will be ignored and will leave in
place the default remote-to-remote copy behaviour (copy via the
host running scp).
*
sshd(8)
: support for platforms that do not allow file descriptor
passing and that also require root privilege for PTY allocation
will be removed in a future release. Affected platforms are known
to include SCO OpenServer 5 and QNX 6 but may include other
similarly old operating systems. This deprecation can be avoided
if the user community for these platforms is able to assist us in
building alternatives, such as avoiding the need for root in PTY
allocation.
Potentially-incompatible changes
--------------------------------
*
ssh(1)
,
sshd(8)
: compression will be less effective as a result
of the change noted below in the "Security" section
*
ssh(1)
: destination usernames entered on the commandline are now
more strictly checked and will refuse usernames that include
backslash and dollar symbols. Usernames that are specified by
the "User" directive in configuration files are not subject to
these restrictions. The motivation for this change is mentioned
below in the "Security" section.
*
sshd(8)
: on platforms that do not support file descriptor passing
and that require root for PTY allocation, the GatewayPorts and
StreamLocalForwarding options are forcibly disabled. The
motivation for this change is discussed below in the "Security"
section.
Changes since OpenSSH 10.5
==========================
This release contains a number of security fixes, several new
features and some small bugfixes.
Security
========
*
sftp(1)
: more strictly validate paths returned from the server to
avoid some cases where a server could return paths that could
manipulate a recursive copy operation into writing outside its
target directory. Report and patch from Junghoon Cho.
*
sshd(8)
: when GSSAPIAuthentication is in use, only store GSSAPI
credentials when authentication has succeeded. Avoids a situation
where credentials from a failed GSSAPIAuthentication attempt may
persist and be made inappropriately available if another
authentication subsequently succeeds. Issue report and patch from
Moritz Theile.
*
sshd(8)
: reset GSSAPIAuthentication before authentication, avoiding
state from one authentication attempt being confused with that of
a later attempt. Report and feedback from Moritz Theile.
*
sshd(8)
,
ssh(1)
: disable LZ77 dictionary coder to mitigate the
side-channel leaks described in "Crossing the Streams: SSH
Plaintext Recovery via a Common Compression Context in
Multiplexed Channels" by Fabian BÃ¤umer and Marcus Brinkmann,
preprint
https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07709
(2026)
A chosen-plaintext attack method exists which makes use of
dictionary-based compression to recover secrets from one channel
by interacting with the SSH session's shared compression
dictionary through another channel.
